population_note_text: Books population (optional, cancelled and post-dated vouchers excluded); Contra excluded throughout. A loan ledger's interest journals are vouchers whose only other ledger lines are its configured interest ledger or ledgers (the client's list of loans) and any ledger the client configures as TDS payable; every other voucher touching the loan ledger is a taken (credit) or repaid (debit) transaction, never classified by ledger name -- except one that both credits and debits the loan ledger, which is listed as the books hold it, not divided into entries.

A voucher listed as both crediting and debiting one loan is in neither total, even where one side reaches the limit; from its date on, an entry on that loan is in it only if its own amount reaches the limit.

findings.title_text: Deductor status for s.194A depends on previous-year turnover
limits_text: An individual/HUF is a s.194A deductor only if the immediately preceding year's turnover from a business exceeded ₹1 crore, or its gross receipts from a profession exceeded ₹50 lakh (s.194A(1) proviso; s.194C Explanation (i)(l)(B)); whether the client carries on a business or a profession is not recorded; the current year's books alone cannot establish this. The previous-year turnover on file is a placeholder, so it is not relied on.
ask_client_text: Confirm previous-year turnover or gross receipts, and whether from a business or a profession.

findings.title_text: Interest to Invented Unknown Seen Lender: whether the TDS seen covers it under s.194A is not computed -- a voucher that both credits and debits the loan carries interest or TDS
limits_text: 1 voucher(s) both credit and debit this loan and carry its interest ledger or a TDS ledger; this test lists each as the books hold it and does not divide it into entries. Their interest (₹0) is shown beside the interest total, not in it; any TDS on them is in the TDS seen on the loan, unless the voucher also posts to another configured loan. The interest crosses the s.194A threshold (₹10,000) with or without it, but whether the TDS seen covers it is not computed: part of the TDS may be on those vouchers (unless each also posts to another configured loan, whose TDS is not counted here), and which interest it covers is not read. This loan is in no clause 21(b) item from this test.
s.40(a)(ia) disallows 30% of the interest on a TDS default; the second proviso removes this if the lender's Form 26A (Rule 31ACB) shows the interest was returned as income.
ask_client_text: The interest credited to Invented Unknown Seen Lender for the year, the TDS deducted on it under s.194A, and the challans showing it was deposited.

limits_text: 1 voucher(s) both credit and debit this loan and carry its interest ledger or a TDS ledger; this test lists each as the books hold it and does not divide it into entries. Their interest (₹5,000) is shown beside the interest total, not in it; any TDS on them is in the TDS seen on the loan, unless the voucher also posts to another configured loan. The interest crosses the s.194A threshold (₹10,000) with that interest and not without it, so whether it crosses is not computed. This loan is in no clause 21(b) item from this test.
s.40(a)(ia) disallows 30% of the interest on a TDS default; the second proviso removes this if the lender's Form 26A (Rule 31ACB) shows the interest was returned as income.
ask_client_text: The interest credited to Invented Crossing Lender for the year, the TDS deducted on it under s.194A, and the challans showing it was deposited.

findings.title_text: Loan ledger both credited and debited in one voucher: listed as the books hold it, not divided into entries by this test (Invented Unknown Seen Lender) (possible s.269SS/269T)
limits_text: This voucher credits the loan ₹200 and debits it ₹1,000. This test does not yet divide a voucher with both sides on one loan into its entries, so it lists it as the books hold it: in no reportable total and not in the s.269SS/269T flag count. Both sides stay in the loan's credits and debits before any filter.
By the voucher's own arithmetic at least ₹200 of the credit is set off against the debit: its other debit lines total less than the credit.
Every entry on this loan dated on or after this voucher is tested on its own amount only: its reportability by the running balance is not computed, and neither is the loan's maximum balance.

Possible s.269T: the voucher's other credit lines include a ledger that is not a bank account (cash, a journal or another ledger). Whether a limit is breached is not computed; this is not in the s.269SS/269T flag count.
It was not compared with this loan's other entries for reversal pairs or repeated narrations.
ask_client_text: Entry by entry, what was taken from the lender, repaid to it, credited as interest or a charge, and withheld as TDS in this voucher, and by what mode (cash, bank, adjustment)? If part of it corrects another part, which?
